title: General words for time, quality and condition
blurb: Place the HESI A2 time words in order (prior, interim, subsequent), tell concurrent from consecutive, and read condition words such as intact, viable and adequate.
question: A care plan says to give two drugs concurrently, schedule three consecutive therapy sessions and confirm the skin is intact before surgery. What happens at the same time, what happens in a row, and what condition is the skin in?

teach.h: When, how often and in what state
teach.body: Formally, these are general academic words that place events in time (order, overlap, frequency, length) or describe the quality and condition of a thing. In plain English: they answer 'When? How often? How long? What shape is it in?' Health instructions are full of them: prior to surgery, consecutive doses, an intact dressing, adequate fluids. HESI A2 traps pair look-alikes such as concurrent/consecutive and sporadic/periodic.

teach.caption: Duration is the length of time something lasts. Obsolete means out of date; inevitable means certain to happen.

items: Stop eating eight hours prior to the test (before).
Subsequent visits will be by video (later ones).
An interim manager runs the unit until a new one is hired (temporary).
The preliminary results were normal (early, not final).
A dark, quiet room is conducive to sleep (favorable to it).
The cause was apparent at once (obvious, in this sentence).

teach.h: Scenario: Daniel reads a therapy plan
teach.body: Daniel Kim, applying to a physical therapist assistant program, shadows at a clinic. The plan reads: 'Prior to each session, check that the incision is intact. Ten consecutive weekday sessions, with periodic strength tests. Pain must stay tolerable.' Daniel decodes it: before each session, confirm the incision is whole; ten sessions in a row; strength tests at regular intervals; pain kept bearable. He notes that consecutive is not concurrent: the sessions do not happen at once.

teach.text: Some time words have two senses, and the sentence decides: contemporary can mean 'at the same time' or 'modern'; apparent can mean 'obvious' or 'seeming.' Never choose a sense the sentence does not support. And sporadic (irregular) is the opposite of periodic (regular), not a synonym.

items: Overlap vs sequence: concurrent = same time; consecutive = in a row.
Frequency and length: sporadic, periodic, temporary, permanent, duration, obsolete, inevitable.
Condition: intact, integrity, viable, feasible, stable, adequate, tolerable, inherent, uniform, conducive.
Look-alikes: conductive, variable, fallible, inherited, contemporary, accurate.

summary: You can now place HESI A2 time words in order, tell concurrent from consecutive and sporadic from periodic, and define the common condition words. You can also reject look-alike distractors such as conductive, inherited and contemporary.

A.q: Do not eat or drink anything for eight hours prior to your fasting blood test on Monday. What is the best definition of the word prior in this sentence?
A.why: Prior (to) means earlier in time; before.

whyNot.2: During means at the same time as the test, not earlier.
whyNot.3: Instead of means in place of; prior is about timing.

A.q: Patients on this medication need periodic liver tests while they continue the treatment. What is the best definition of the word periodic in this sentence?
A.why: Periodic means happening at regular intervals.

whyNot.0: Random timing is sporadic, the opposite pattern.

A.q: A temporary cast will protect the broken wrist until the swelling goes down. What is the best definition of the word temporary in this sentence?
A.why: Temporary means lasting for a limited time; the cast is used only until the swelling goes down.

whyNot.3: Waterproof is a topic fit for casts, but temporary describes time.

B.q: The patient's condition is stable, so she will move from intensive care to a regular room tonight. What is the best definition of the word stable in this sentence?
B.why: Stable means not likely to change or get worse; steady.

whyNot.0: Leaving intensive care fits improvement, but stable means not changing, not getting better quickly.
whyNot.2: Critical is the opposite of stable.
whyNot.3: Uncertain is close to the opposite of stable.

B.q: The cause of the leak was apparent as soon as the plumber saw the cracked pipe under the sink. What is the best definition of the word apparent in this sentence?
B.why: Here apparent means clearly visible or understood: the cause was obvious as soon as he saw the pipe.

whyNot.0: Hidden is the opposite of obvious.
whyNot.1: Unusual describes rarity, not how easy it is to see.
whyNot.3: Repairs are costly, a topic fit, but apparent describes visibility.

B.q: Mix the powdered drink until the solution is uniform in color with no streaks. What is the best definition of the word uniform in this sentence?
B.why: As an adjective, uniform means the same throughout; consistent.

whyNot.0: One-sided is unilateral, a look-alike prefix word.
whyNot.1: Unique means one of a kind, another uni- word.
whyNot.2: Informal is a look-alike ending; it means casual.

C.q: The physical therapist adjusted the stretch until the pain was tolerable for the patient. What is the best definition of the word tolerable in this sentence?
C.why: Tolerable means able to be endured; bearable.

whyNot.0: Accepting is tolerant, a look-alike that describes a person.
whyNot.3: Treatable is a topic fit, but tolerable means able to be endured.

C.q: Which word means happening at the same time?
C.why: Concurrent means happening at the same time.

whyNot.0: Consecutive means one after another, the classic look-alike.
whyNot.3: Continual means happening again and again, not simultaneously.

C.q: The pharmacist checks that every label is accurate before handing over a prescription. What is the best definition of the word accurate in this sentence?
C.why: Accurate means correct; free of error.

whyNot.1: A label should be readable, a topic fit, but accurate means correct.
whyNot.2: Current means up to date; a label can be current and still wrong.

reteach.title: Read it like a train schedule
reteach.question: A train schedule tells you what leaves first, what runs at the same time, and what is delayed. How do the time words work the same way?

blocks.body: Trains on two platforms leaving at 8:00 are concurrent. The 8:00, 8:30 and 9:00 on one track are consecutive. A train every 30 minutes is periodic; one that shows up whenever it likes is sporadic. The board says the 9:00 is delayed, so an interim bus runs. The bus is temporary; the subsequent train will restore service. Read any time word by asking where it sits on the schedule.

blocks.text: Two trains at once are concurrent, not consecutive. Back to back is consecutive.

explain.body: Prior and preliminary come before; interim is in between; subsequent comes after.

test.q: Which word means coming after something else?
test.why: Subsequent means coming after something else.

whyNot.0: Preceding means coming before, the opposite.
whyNot.1: Simultaneous means at the same time.
whyNot.3: Subservient means overly obedient, a look-alike.

explain.body: Periodic events happen at regular intervals. Sporadic events happen at irregular, scattered times. Perpetual means never ending.

test.q: Which word describes events that happen at irregular, scattered times?
test.why: Sporadic means happening at irregular, scattered times.

whyNot.0: Periodic means at regular intervals, the opposite pattern.
whyNot.2: Spastic describes muscle spasms, a look-alike.

explain.body: Intact (undamaged), viable (able to work or live), feasible (possible to do), adequate (enough), tolerable (bearable).

test.q: Which word means possible to do; practical?
test.why: Feasible means possible to do; practical.

whyNot.0: Fallible means capable of making mistakes.
whyNot.3: Visible means able to be seen.

explain.body: Conducive (to) means favorable, making an outcome likely. Conductive means able to carry heat or electricity.

test.q: Select the word that best completes the sentence: Bright phone screens late at night are not ____ to restful sleep.
test.why: Conducive to means favorable to; bright screens do not help sleep.

whyNot.0: Conductive means carrying heat or electricity, the look-alike.
whyNot.1: Conclusive means settling a question; it does not take 'to sleep.'
whyNot.3: Coercive means using force; screens do not force sleep.
